title: Storage

header.html: Implement storage classes and dynamic volume provisioning; Configure volume types, access modes and reclaim policies; Manage persistent volumes and persistent volume claims

toc.title: Use a PVC in a Pod

html:
1The storage objects

Object Scope Job
Volume (in a Pod spec) Pod storage mounted into containers; some types live and die with the Pod
PersistentVolume (PV) cluster a piece of storage, made by an admin or by a provisioner
PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) namespace a request for storage by a user; binds to one PV
StorageClass (SC) cluster a recipe for creating PVs on demand (dynamic provisioning)

The flow: a Pod references a PVC; the PVC binds to a PV (an existing one that fits, or one the StorageClass creates); the kubelet mounts the PV into the Pod.

2Volume types you must know

Type Lifetime and use
emptyDir created empty when the Pod starts, deleted with the Pod; scratch space or sharing between containers of one Pod (Lab 10.5)
hostPath a directory of the node; survives Pod deletion but ties data to one node; avoid except for tests and node agents
configMap, secret, projected configuration files (Module 5)
persistentVolumeClaim durable storage through a PVC
nfs, CSI-driver volumes network or cloud storage

3Static provisioning (admin creates the PV)

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata: {name: pv-manual}
spec:
  capacity: {storage: 2Gi}
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: manual
  hostPath: {path: /mnt/data}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: claim, namespace: st2}
spec:
  storageClassName: manual
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}

A claim binds to a PV only when all of these fit: the same storageClassName; the PV offers (contains) every access mode the claim requests; the PV capacity is at least the requested size (a 1Gi claim can bind a 2Gi PV, and then owns all of it). A PV binds to only one claim. A PVC is namespaced; a PV is not.

If the PVC omits storageClassName, the default StorageClass is used. Writing storageClassName: "" means "no class, bind only to a PV without a class".

4Dynamic provisioning with a StorageClass

apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: retain-sc
  annotations: {storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true"}   # makes it the default
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
reclaimPolicy: Retain
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
allowVolumeExpansion: false
Field Meaning
provisioner the driver that creates volumes
reclaimPolicy what happens to the PV when its claim is deleted: Delete (default for SC) or Retain
volumeBindingMode Immediate creates the volume as soon as the PVC exists; WaitForFirstConsumer waits until a Pod uses the PVC (so the volume lands on the right node)
allowVolumeExpansion whether a PVC may be enlarged later

WaitForFirstConsumer explains a PVC that shows Pending with no error: it is waiting for a Pod. Create the Pod and it binds. There must be exactly one default class; change defaults with k annotate sc <name> storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class=true --overwrite (and =false on the old one) (Lab 10.3). Look: k get sc marks the default with (default).

5Access modes and reclaim policies

Access mode Short Meaning
ReadWriteOnce RWO read-write by one node
ReadOnlyMany ROX read-only by many nodes
ReadWriteMany RWX read-write by many nodes (needs a driver that supports it, such as NFS)
ReadWriteOncePod RWOP read-write by a single Pod
Reclaim policy After the PVC is deleted
Delete the PV and the underlying storage are deleted
Retain the PV stays, status Released, data kept; an admin must clean it before reuse

Change the policy of an existing PV: k patch pv <name> -p '{"spec":{"persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy":"Retain"}}'. Find the PV of a claim: k -n ns get pvc name -o jsonpath='{.spec.volumeName}' (Lab 10.4). The StorageClass reclaimPolicy only affects PVs created afterwards.

6Use a PVC in a Pod

spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: vol, mountPath: /data}
  volumes:
  - name: vol
    persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: data}

The PVC must be in the same namespace as the Pod. Data written to a bound PVC survives deletion of the Pod.

7Troubleshooting storage (break-and-fix patterns)

Symptom Look at Typical cause
Pod Pending, event "unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims" or "persistentvolumeclaim not found" k describe pod, k get pvc PVC missing, wrong name or wrong namespace
PVC Pending, event "storageclass ... not found" k describe pvc, k get sc class name typo (Lab 10.6)
PVC Pending, no matching PV k describe pvc, k get pv access mode not offered by the PV, size too big, class mismatch (Lab 10.7)
PVC Pending and nothing else k get sc WaitForFirstConsumer: create the Pod
PV Released k get pv claim deleted with Retain; remove claimRef to reuse

A claim's storageClassName, accessModes and size cannot be changed on a bound or pending claim in the ways these tasks need: delete and recreate the claim (and the Pod using it).

8Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m10 -->

Lab 10.1: dynamic pvc

Domain: Storage | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-01-dynamic-pvc)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace st1, create a PersistentVolumeClaim data requesting 1Gi with access mode ReadWriteOnce, using the cluster's default StorageClass. Then create a Pod writer (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that mounts the claim at /data and write the text hello to the file /data/test.txt in that Pod.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n st1 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: data}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: writer}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: vol, mountPath: /data}
  volumes:
  - name: vol
    persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: data}
Y
kubectl -n st1 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/writer --timeout=120s
kubectl -n st1 exec writer -- sh -c 'echo hello > /data/test.txt'
kubectl -n st1 get pvc data

Lab 10.2: static pv pvc

Domain: Storage | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-02-static-pv-pvc)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Create a PersistentVolume pv-manual with capacity 2Gi, access mode ReadWriteOnce, reclaim policy Retain, StorageClass name manual and the host path /mnt/data. In the namespace st2, create a PersistentVolumeClaim claim requesting 1Gi, ReadWriteOnce, StorageClass manual. The claim must be bound to pv-manual.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata: {name: pv-manual}
spec:
  capacity: {storage: 2Gi}
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: manual
  hostPath: {path: /mnt/data}
Y
kubectl -n st2 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: claim}
spec:
  storageClassName: manual
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
Y
sleep 3
kubectl -n st2 get pvc claim

Lab 10.3: storageclass default

Domain: Storage | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-03-storageclass-default)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Create a StorageClass named retain-sc with the provisioner rancher.io/local-path, reclaim policy Retain and volume binding mode WaitForFirstConsumer. Make retain-sc the default StorageClass of the cluster and remove the default mark from the class standard (there must be exactly one default class).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: retain-sc
  annotations: {storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true"}
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
reclaimPolicy: Retain
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
Y
kubectl annotate sc standard storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class=false --overwrite
kubectl get sc

Lab 10.4: reclaim retain

Domain: Storage | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-04-reclaim-retain)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace st4, the PersistentVolumeClaim keepme is bound to a dynamically provisioned PersistentVolume whose reclaim policy is Delete. The data must survive even if the claim is deleted. Change the reclaim policy of that PersistentVolume to Retain. Do not change the claim or the StorageClass.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

pv=$(kubectl -n st4 get pvc keepme -o jsonpath='{.spec.volumeName}')
kubectl get pv $pv
kubectl patch pv $pv -p '{"spec":{"persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy":"Retain"}}'
kubectl get pv $pv

Lab 10.5: emptydir shared

Domain: Storage | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-05-emptydir-shared)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace st5, create a Pod pair with two containers that share a temporary volume: the container producer (busybox, writes the text ready to /shared/status and then sleeps) and the container consumer (busybox, sleeps). Both mount the volume at /shared. The volume must be an emptyDir (it is deleted with the Pod). Prove that consumer can read the file.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n st5 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: pair}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: producer
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo ready > /shared/status; sleep 3600"]
    volumeMounts: [{name: scratch, mountPath: /shared}]
  - name: consumer
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts: [{name: scratch, mountPath: /shared}]
  volumes:
  - name: scratch
    emptyDir: {}
Y
kubectl -n st5 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/pair --timeout=120s
kubectl -n st5 exec pair -c consumer -- cat /shared/status

Lab 10.6: fix pending pvc

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-06-fix-pending-pvc)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace st6, the Pod app is stuck Pending because its PersistentVolumeClaim app-data does not bind. Find the cause and fix it so the Pod runs with the claim bound. Keep the names app and app-data, the size 1Gi and ReadWriteOnce. (A claim's StorageClass cannot be edited in place; recreate what is needed.)

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n st6 describe pod app | grep -i -A2 "FailedScheduling"
kubectl -n st6 describe pvc app-data | grep -i -A2 events
kubectl get sc
kubectl -n st6 delete pod app --force --grace-period 0
kubectl -n st6 delete pvc app-data
kubectl -n st6 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: app-data}
spec:
  storageClassName: standard
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: app}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts: [{name: vol, mountPath: /data}]
  volumes:
  - name: vol
    persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: app-data}
Y
kubectl -n st6 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/app --timeout=120s

Lab 10.7: fix access mode

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-07-fix-access-mode)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

The PersistentVolume pv-share offers 1Gi with access mode ReadWriteMany in the StorageClass shared. In the namespace st7, the claim share (StorageClass shared, 1Gi) stays Pending. Fix the claim so that it binds to pv-share. Do not change the PersistentVolume.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n st7 describe pvc share | tail -5
kubectl get pv pv-share
kubectl -n st7 delete pvc share
kubectl -n st7 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: share}
spec:
  storageClassName: shared
  accessModes: [ReadWriteMany]
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
Y
sleep 4
kubectl -n st7 get pvc share

Lab 10.8: pvc persists

Domain: Storage | Points: 6 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-08-pvc-persists)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace st8, the PVC notes (1Gi, default StorageClass) and the Pod first that mounts it at /notes already exist, and first wrote the file /notes/keep.txt. Delete the Pod first and create a new Pod second (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that mounts the same claim at /notes, so that the data written by first is still there.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n st8 delete pod first --force --grace-period 0
kubectl -n st8 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: second}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts: [{name: vol, mountPath: /notes}]
  volumes:
  - name: vol
    persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: notes}
Y
kubectl -n st8 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/second --timeout=120s
kubectl -n st8 exec second -- cat /notes/keep.txt

Lab 10.9: released pv reuse

Domain: Storage | Points: 8 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-09-released-pv-reuse)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

The PersistentVolume pv-archive (1Gi, StorageClass archive, reclaim policy Retain) was used by a claim that has been deleted, so the PV shows Released and cannot be bound again. In the namespace st9, create a new PVC restored (StorageClass archive, 1Gi, ReadWriteOnce) and make it bind to pv-archive. Do not create a new PV.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl get pv pv-archive
kubectl patch pv pv-archive -p '{"spec":{"claimRef":null}}'
kubectl -n st9 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: restored}
spec:
  storageClassName: archive
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
Y
sleep 4
kubectl -n st9 get pvc restored

Lab 10.10: hostpath volume

Domain: Storage | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-10-hostpath-volume)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace st10, create a Pod logger (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that mounts the directory /var/log/app-data of the node cka-worker at /logs in the container. The directory must be created on the node if it does not exist. Run the Pod on cka-worker, and write the file /logs/hello.txt with the text from-pod; the file must then exist on the node.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n st10 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: logger}
spec:
  nodeName: cka-worker
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts: [{name: logs, mountPath: /logs}]
  volumes:
  - name: logs
    hostPath: {path: /var/log/app-data, type: DirectoryOrCreate}
Y
kubectl -n st10 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/logger --timeout=120s
kubectl -n st10 exec logger -- sh -c 'echo from-pod > /logs/hello.txt'
ssh cka-worker 'cat /var/log/app-data/hello.txt'

Lab 10.11: pvc readonly

Domain: Storage | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-11-pvc-readonly)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace st11, the PVC shared (1Gi) is bound and holds the file /data/seed.txt. Create a Pod reader (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that mounts the claim at /data read-only, so the seed file can be read but nothing can be written.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n st11 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: reader}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts: [{name: vol, mountPath: /data, readOnly: true}]
  volumes:
  - name: vol
    persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: shared}
Y
kubectl -n st11 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/reader --timeout=120s
kubectl -n st11 exec reader -- cat /data/seed.txt

Lab 10.12: statefulset claims

Domain: Storage | Points: 8 | Time: about 9 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-12-statefulset-claims)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace st12, create a StatefulSet store with 2 replicas of nginx:alpine and a headless Service store (port 80). Each replica must get its own 1Gi ReadWriteOnce volume mounted at /usr/share/nginx/html, created from a volumeClaimTemplates entry named www. At the end the claims www-store-0 and www-store-1 must be Bound.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n st12 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: store}
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector: {app: store}
  ports: [{port: 80}]
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata: {name: store}
spec:
  serviceName: store
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: store}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: store}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:alpine
        volumeMounts: [{name: www, mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html}]
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata: {name: www}
    spec:
      accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
      resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
Y
kubectl -n st12 rollout status statefulset store --timeout=180s
kubectl -n st12 get pvc

<!-- /LABS -->

9Recall questions

R1What decides whether a PVC binds to a PV?

Show the answer

Same StorageClass, the PV offers all requested access modes, and the PV capacity is at least the requested size.

R2What does volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer do?

Show the answer

It delays creating and binding the volume until a Pod uses the PVC.

R3What happens to a PV with Retain when its PVC is deleted?

Show the answer

The PV stays with status Released and keeps its data.

R4Which volume type is deleted when the Pod is deleted?

Show the answer

emptyDir.

R5How do you make a StorageClass the default?

Show the answer

Annotate it storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class=true (and remove the mark from the old default).

R6Can a PV be bound by two claims?

Show the answer

No, one claim only.

R7A PVC requests ReadWriteOnce but the only PV offers ReadWriteMany. What happens?

Show the answer

It stays Pending: the PV does not offer the requested mode.

R8What is the effect of a missing storageClassName in a PVC?

Show the answer

The default StorageClass is used.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Objects PV (cluster), PVC (namespace), StorageClass (recipe)
Bind rules class + access modes + size (PV >= claim)
Dynamic StorageClass with provisioner; default class by annotation
Binding mode WaitForFirstConsumer = Pending until a Pod uses it
Reclaim Delete or Retain; patch the PV to change it
Access modes RWO, ROX, RWX, RWOP
emptyDir lives with the Pod; hostPath ties data to a node
Fix a claim delete and recreate it
